- When sentiment is strongly positive (≥ 0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–3% for next period.  
- When sentiment is strongly negative (≤ 0.33) or volatile, model often underestimates; increase forecast by 1–3% to account for downward surprise.  
- If model shows sharp upward spike in forecast (e.g., >10% from prior), reduce by 5–10% in next period to avoid overshoot.  
- If true outcome shows mean reversion (e.g., 3–5 consecutive days below 65–70), model often fails to adjust; apply downward bias of 2–5% for next 2–3 periods.  
- For 30-day horizon, model frequently overreacts to recent sentiment swings; smooth forecast by averaging last 5–7 days’ values before applying sentiment-weighted adjustment.  
- If sentiment history shows alternating highs/lows (e.g., 0.67, 0.33, 0.67), model tends to lag; add 1–2% lagged sentiment adjustment to forecast.
